title: CATL
summary: The world's largest EV battery maker, now exporting both cells and its manufacturing model.
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

CATL supplied roughly 38% of global EV batteries in 2024, more than any competitor, and has expanded from cells into licensing its technology to other manufacturers. It launched a sodium-ion product in 2025 aimed at cold climates and cost-sensitive segments, alongside faster-charging LFP chemistries. Growth now depends on European and North American plants, where permitting, tariffs and local-content rules matter as much as chemistry.

Technology Exposure

  • LFP and sodium-ion cells for mass-market vehicles.
  • Grid-scale storage systems and licensing of cell technology.

What To Watch

  • Utilisation and pricing in a oversupplied cell market.
  • Progress of European plants under tariff and local-content pressure.

Record Notes

Editorial brief compiled 18 November 2026 from company disclosures, agency publications and press reporting. Figures are as reported by those sources and have not been independently audited; no live market data is used.

businessMeaning: Battery cost is the constraint that decides whether electrification reaches mid-market fleets; CATL's scale sets the reference price.
investmentLens: Volume leadership plus licensing is a strong position, but cell oversupply and customer vertical integration cap pricing power.
